The OPf_PARENS fixtures (issue 01a16602-5f1a), held as probes: every
snippet of internal/parseoracle/testdata/parens/fixtures.txt and gaps.txt,
which TestParenFlagMatchesPerlOPfPARENS compares op by op. perl keeps one
boolean bit, OPf_PARENS (P in Concise), on the op a source paren enclosed;
a pair the syntax requires -- `$f->(...)`, `not (...)`, a list slice's
`(...)[...]` -- sets no bit, and psc records it as SyntaxParen, not Paren.
Each row's comment quotes perl 5.44.0's -MO=Concise.

=== a declared list
my ($a, $b) = @_;
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> ex-list lKPRM* ->4

=== a declared list and a list assignment
our ($p, $q);
($p, $q) = (1, 2);
--- facts
faithful
# -     <1> ex-list vKP ->2
# -        <1> ex-list lKP ->6
# -        <1> ex-list lKPRM* ->9

=== a declared one-element list
my ($x) = @_;
--- facts
faithful
# -           <0> padsv[$x:1,2] sPRM*/LVINTRO ->-
# the ex-list over it is lK, with no P

=== a localised one-element list
our $x;
local ($x) = 1;
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-rv2sv sKPRM*/LVINTRO,1 ->-

=== a lexical in parens
my $x;
my $z = ($x);
--- facts
faithful
# 5        <0> padsv[$x:1,3] sP ->6

=== a package variable in parens
our $x;
my $z = ($x);
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> ex-rv2sv sKP/1 ->4

=== a lexical in doubled parens
my $x;
my $z = (($x));
--- facts
faithful
# 5        <0> padsv[$x:1,3] sP ->6, as with one pair

=== a comparison in doubled parens as a call argument
sub ok {}
our $y;
ok((($y eq "x")));
--- facts
faithful
# 8           <2> seq sKPM/2 ->9, as with one pair

=== a comparison in parens as a call argument
sub ok {}
our $y;
ok(($y eq "x"));
--- facts
faithful
# 8           <2> seq sKPM/2 ->9

=== a call's parens around a parenthesised constant
print ((1))+2;
--- facts
faithful
# 4           <$> const[IV 1] sP ->5

=== a call's parens around a constant
print (1)+2;
--- facts
faithful
# 4           <$> const[IV 1] s ->5: print's pair is its call parens

=== a parenthesised list as a call's argument
sub f {}
f((1,2));
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-list lKPM ->8

=== a qw list
my @a = qw(a b);
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> ex-list lKP ->6

=== a one-word qw list
my @a = qw(a);
--- facts
faithful
# 4           <$> const[PV "a"] sP ->5

=== a qw list in parens
my @a = (qw(a b));
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> ex-list lKP ->6, as without the parens

=== return of a parenthesised list
sub r {
  return (1, 2);
}
--- facts
faithful
# -        <@> return KP ->-: return absorbed the list, and no list op is left

=== return of a doubly parenthesised list
sub s {
  return ((1, 2));
}
--- facts
faithful
# -        <@> return KP ->-

=== return of a parenthesised constant
sub t {
  return (1);
}
--- facts
faithful
# 2           <$> const[IV 1] sP ->3

=== if, else and do blocks
our $x;
if ($x) {
  my $y = 1;
  $y++;
}
else {
  my $y = 2;
  $y++;
}
my $r = do { my $z = 1; $z };
--- facts
faithful
# c           <@> leave vKP ->d, u           <@> leave vKP ->d,
# k           <@> leave sKP ->l and -     <1> null vKP/1 ->d over the if's
# `and`: structural, excluded. A one-statement block is `scope vK`, no P.

=== for and while loops
for my $i (1, 2) {
  my $y = ($i);
  $y++;
}
our $x;
while ($x) {
  $x--;
  1;
}
--- facts
faithful
# 8                    <0> padsv[$i:2,6] sP ->9
# g     <2> leaveloop vKP/2 ->h and -              <@> lineseq vKP ->-, on
# each loop: structural, excluded

=== an arrow call's argument
my $f = sub {};
our $x;
$f->($x);
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-rv2sv sKM/1 ->8: the pair is the call's

=== an arrow call's argument in doubled parens
my $f = sub {};
our $x;
$f->(($x));
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-rv2sv sKPM/1 ->8

=== an arrow call's arguments
my $f = sub {};
$f->(1, 2);
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> ex-list K ->a: the pair is the call's

=== an arrow call's arguments in doubled parens
my $f = sub {};
$f->((1, 2));
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-list lKPM ->9

=== an arrow call with no arguments
my $f = sub {};
$f->();
--- facts
faithful
# -        <1> ex-list K ->8

=== not's parenthesised operand
our $a;
my $r = not ($a == 1);
--- facts
faithful
# 5           <2> eq sK/2 ->6: the pair is not's

=== not's operand in doubled parens
our $a;
my $r = not (($a == 1));
--- facts
faithful
# 5           <2> eq sKP/2 ->6

=== a parenthesised not
our $x;
my $r = (not $x);
--- facts
faithful
# 4        <1> not sKP/1 ->5

=== a list slice of an array
my @a;
my @x = (@a)[0];
--- facts
faithful
# 9                 <0> padav[@a:1,3] l ->a: the pair is the slice's

=== a list slice of an array in doubled parens
my @a;
my @x = ((@a))[0];
--- facts
faithful
# 9                 <0> padav[@a:1,3] lP ->a

=== a list slice of a list
my $x = (1,2,3)[1];
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-list lK ->9

=== a list slice of a list in doubled parens
my $x = ((1,2,3))[1];
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-list lKP ->9

=== a list slice of stat in doubled parens
my $x = ((stat "/"))[2];
--- facts
faithful
# 7              <1> stat lKP/1 ->8; `(stat "/")[2]` is stat lK

=== a list slice of caller in doubled parens
my $x = ((caller))[2];
--- facts
faithful
# 6              <0> caller[t2] lP ->7

=== a list slice of a parenthesised element and a comma
my $x = ((0),)[0];
--- facts
faithful
# 6              <$> const[IV 0] sP ->7; `(0,)[0]` is const[IV 0] s

=== an arrow call's parenthesised argument and a comma
my $f = sub {};
$f->((0),);
--- facts
faithful
# 7           <$> const[IV 0] sPM ->8: the inner pair is the 0's

=== a parenthesised hash key
my %h;
my $v = $h{(1)};
--- facts
faithful
# 5           <+> multideref($h{"1"}) sK ->6: the key's const is folded
# into the multideref, and no op carries P

=== a negated parenthesised constant
my $v = -(1);
--- facts
faithful
# 3        <$> const[IV -1] s/FOLD ->4

=== a concatenation with a parenthesised constant
my $v = "a" . ("b");
--- facts
faithful
# 3        <$> const[PV "ab"] s/FOLD ->4

=== a parenthesised element before an arrow subscript
sub g {
  my $v = ($_[0])->[0];
}
--- facts
faithful
# -           <1> ex-aelem sK/2 ->3
# 2              <+> multideref($_[0][0]) sK ->3: the aelem is nulled
# into the multideref, and no op carries P
